final_candidates.decision_summary: D473 is an essential charged residue in the central substrate binding cavity; substituting with alanine abolishes cation transport while maintaining normal protein folding and membrane localization.
E454 is a key acidic active-site residue involved in organic cation recognition; alanine mutation disrupts substrate transport without compromising structural integrity.
Y360 forms essential aromatic binding interactions in the translocation pore; mutating it to alanine severely impairs transport activity while preserving overall protein stability.

stop_reason.detail: Top 3 candidates represent optimal active-site charge/aromatic modifications that selectively abolish transport function while preserving folding.

history.rationale: D473 in TM11 is the primary acidic residue essential for organic cation substrate binding; alanine substitution neutralizes charge and abolishes transport while retaining cell-surface expression.
Retain top candidate targeting essential substrate interaction residue D473 without structural disruption.
D473 is a essential charge residue in the substrate binding cavity; high AlphaMissense LOF prediction supports loss of transport capability.
D473N neutralizes the critical substrate-binding negative charge while preserving side-chain hydrogen bonding capacity and protein folding.
Retain charge-neutralizing mutation at primary binding residue D473.
D473N removes the negative charge while preserving shape, giving moderate LOF without causing misfolding.
D397 is a conserved TM8 acidic residue involved in substrate translocation and charge interactions; mutating to Ala disrupts transport activity without destroying fold.
Retain alanine substitution at critical catalytic/binding residue D397.
D397A shows ambiguous LOF prediction, ranking lower than core active site charge mutations.
D397N eliminates the ionic charge required for cation transport while maintaining side-chain size and protein stability.
Retain isosteric amide substitution at conserved charge site D397.
D397N is classified as benign by AlphaMissense, indicating minimal effect on transport activity.

rejection.reason: D397N is classified as benign by AlphaMissense, indicating minimal effect on transport activity.

history.rationale: W216 in TM4 forms key cation-pi interactions in the substrate binding pocket; Ala substitution severely reduces transport function.
Retain candidate disrupting cation-pi substrate interaction at TM4 Trp216.
W216 provides crucial aromatic substrate capping; pathogenic LOF score confirms functional importance.
Y360 in TM7 contributes critical aromatic substrate-binding interactions; mutating to Ala abolishes substrate affinity while preserving helical structure.
Retain candidate disrupting central aromatic cavity residue Y360.
Y360 forms essential aromatic binding interactions in the central pore; strong LOF prediction indicates transport impairment.
E454 is a conserved acidic residue in TM10 involved in substrate pathway proton/charge coupling, crucial for transport mechanism.
Retain candidate neutralizing charged cavity residue E454.
E454 is a critical active site carboxylate involved in cation recognition; strong LOF score confirms high impact on function.
R485 is part of the conserved intracellular salt-bridge network involved in transport dynamics; Ala mutation impairs substrate turnover.
Retain candidate targeting positively charged substrate transport pathway residue R485.
R485 is a conserved basic residue in the translocation path; high LOF score supports functional disruption.
R171 in cytoplasmic loop Motif A plays a functional role in the transport cycle conformational changes without destabilizing the transmembrane core.
Retain candidate mutating extracellular loop / cavity access residue R171.
R171A shows moderate LOF score, keeping it behind primary active site candidates.
D425 in TM9/10 contributes to the hydrophilic substrate pore environment; mutation impairs substrate translocation.
Retain candidate neutralizing conserved aspartate D425.
D425A displays a very low LOF score (0.120), indicating it is functionally neutral for substrate transport.

rejection.reason: D425A displays a very low LOF score (0.120), indicating it is functionally neutral for substrate transport.
